content.header: The hard part wasn't the design.
content.subhead: Standardizing fifty-six state forms into one was an information architecture problem. Getting fifty-six jurisdictions to agree to it was the real work.
content.p1: I thought the win would be a leaner form. It was the opposite. Every state built its form for a reason, and none of them wanted to give it up. So I kept every state's fields and made them optional for everyone. No one lost anything; they gained a shared spine underneath.
content.p2: Then I showed each office what that trade actually buys. Once the data is standardized, the system can read it and surface what needs attention on its own. Fifty-six separate spreadsheets never could.
content.p3: None of this was a pitch. Before I asked a single office to give anything up, the whole thing was designed and mapped, every section, every state, every view. The ask was credible because the work was already done.
content.close: BARD reaches initial operating capability with the Coast Guard in spring 2027. In build and testing now.
